author: Bobby Grayson
description: Sys.terminate (Leanactors/Sys.lean:150-156 at dacf642) builds { cfg, next, links, signals, monitors, downs } and never mentions timers, so the structure default [] applies. Consequence: a worker crash silently disarms a watchdog's pending timeout (Watchdog example). SysProps.lean records this as @[simp] terminate_timers and gives Frame p no timers clause (only Grows tracks timers). Builder did not change Sys.lean because it would alter the bounded-checker state counts quoted in README/examples (10365 for watchdog etc). Integrator may add timers := s.timers to terminate, re-run the checkers, and then Frame can gain a timers clause and terminate_timers becomes an equation instead of [].
title: Finding, not fixed: Sys.terminate in Leanactors/Sys.lean omits the timers field, so the structure default applies and every pending timer is dropped whenever any actor dies; proved as terminate_timers : (s.terminate p r).timers = [] (rfl). Frame has no timers clause for this reason while Grows does
